unblock.condition: a WorkBuddy client reachable from the machine running the verification — or a documented configuration format for it, if the acceptance is to be automated against a stub
unblock.then: install the projection, connect, and run the contract in the order listed in ../README.md; every field below becomes measurable in the same way the Codex fields were
unblock.what_must_not_be_done_instead: writing any of these fields as verified because WorkBuddy is expected to speak MCP. Expected compatibility is not a measurement

mcp_connected.unblock: the client, installed, pointed at a deployment

auth_verified.unblock: the client, installed; requires both a successful session and a refused negative control

tool_catalog_verified.unblock: a connected session whose received tool names can be compared against the deployment's catalog

read_flow_verified.unblock: a connected session that can really invoke a read use case

write_flow_verified.unblock: a connected session that can really invoke a write use case, through admission

durable_job_disconnect_verified.unblock: a connected session that can be disconnected while a durable job runs

reconnect_verified.unblock: a connected session that can be closed and reopened

multi_session_isolation_verified.unblock: two concurrently running sessions of this client

notification_pull_verified.unblock: a connected session that can read events and their delivery receipts

notification_push_verified.unblock: a connected session that this deployment can be made to push to; if the client turns out to have no push path, this becomes unsupported rather than blocked, and the degradation ladder in ../README.md applies

plugin_install_verified.unblock: the client's own plugin-install path, which cannot be exercised without the client
